clue.text: Sign of good conduct — after punishment ?

explanation.surface: A badge earned for behaving well, awarded only after a spell of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: A soldier may win a chevron for good conduct, while a flogging leaves weals on the back; the one word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron on a sleeve can reward good conduct, and a lash leaves a long weal, both called by this word.

clue.text: Dry measures include one of these parts

parts.note: sec is dry, of wine

indicators.note: the dry and the measures together take the one inside them

parts.note: tons are measures of weight
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Measures of dry goods include one of these divisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts I inside SEC + TONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A document or object is divided into segments, each a piece of the whole.

clue.text: Hastened to continue to supply capital

parts.note: ran means hurried
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to keep supplies going to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the capital city of Burma until 2005.

clue.text: Soldier meets engineer returning from ship

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

indicators.note: returning means the letters for engineer are read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A soldier meets an engineer coming back from his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) 'returning' becomes ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A privately owned armed vessel licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: States carry out loveless acts

indicators.note: the word States carries the next piece inside it, as a vessel holds its load
love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so the word out loses its O

parts.note: taken as written before losing its letter

explanation.surface: Governments carry through acts with no affection in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry' puts UT (OUT made 'loveless' by dropping the O) inside STATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws passed by a legislature are formally called its acts, the written statutes of a parliament.

clue.text: A lot of wine and game given to writer in Kent

parts.note: a tun is a large cask of wine
bridge is a card game
H G Wells, the writer

explanation.surface: Plenty of wine and a game of cards laid on for an author in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNBRIDGE WELLS is a spa town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentish spa town is a place found in that county.

clue.text: In the end, many form a language

indicators.note: the many goes inside the end

parts.note: the tail is the end of something
M, the Roman thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: In the end, lots of people form one language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally', but it puts M (many) in TAIL (end).
explanation.definitionFit: A Dravidian tongue spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Hides his requirements with gin ?

parts.note: hides are animal skins this hunter wants, and a gin is a snare he uses to get them

explanation.surface: Someone conceals his needs with a glass of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like a verb and 'gin' like a drink; they are pelts and a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter who catches animals for their fur sets snares and sells the skins.

clue.text: A Frenchman's is seen in place of poetry

indicators.note: the French word is placed inside the word for place

parts.note: to set is to place
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is spotted in a poetic setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Frenchman's is' means the French word for 'is', EST, which goes inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-line stanza, such as the last six lines of a sonnet, is a piece of verse.

clue.text: No killer's weapons ?

parts.note: these weapons are named for saving life, the opposite of what a killer wants, yet they are coshes

explanation.surface: Weapons no murderer would carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a club or cosh, a weapon, yet it describes something that saves life, which no killer would want.
explanation.definitionFit: Short weighted clubs carried for self-defence go by this name, as do buoyancy aids.

clue.text: State term

explanation.definitionFit: A state is the condition something is in, and a term of a contract is one of its conditions.

clue.text: A division of people's resources

indicators.note: the letter A splits the word for people's in two, making a division of it

parts.note: men's ... belonging to people

explanation.surface: A share of what the public owns is set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division of' has A dividing MEN'S, giving ME-A-NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's means are their money and assets, the resources they live on.

clue.text: Detach made-up tie also

indicators.note: something made up is invented, so the letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Remove the ready-tied bow tie as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made-up' rearranges TIE and ALSO. The OCR text reads 'tic', but the anagram needs 'tie', a pre-tied bow tie being a made-up tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to set it apart, cut off from the rest.

clue.text: It might keep a convalescent patient

definitions.text: It might keep a convalescent patient

parts.words: It might keep a convalescent patient
parts.note: a recovering patient who falls ill again has to stay on in hospital

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a recovering patient in their hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' reads as caring for the patient; the patient is in fact kept in hospital because the illness has come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback in which an illness returns after improvement keeps the sufferer from being discharged.

clue.text: A hundred in love, just for the time being

indicators.note: the hundred goes inside the word for love, so in means placed within

parts.note: love in tennis is a score of nothing, that is none
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred lovers, but only for now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for the nonce means for the present occasion only, a single use and no more.

clue.text: Not green for "Go " for this bird

parts.note: red is the traffic light that is not green
to go is to start

explanation.surface: Name of a bird that stops at red rather than going on green.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a traffic light; RED is simply the colour that is not green.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European songbird of the thrush family with a red tail.

clue.text: Excursion passages for old fliers

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
lanes are narrow passages

explanation.surface: Trips along passageways for veteran pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: Early aircraft with three stacked wings, such as the First World War Fokker.

clue.text: Lock holds Lee up, being without timber

indicators.note: the lock holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lock of hair keeps Lee upright though without any wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LEE into EEL, which TRESS 'holds' as TR-EEL-ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Land with no woodland is bare of trees.

clue.text: Hypocrite with Heep's air .. possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged in another way

parts.note: the possessive 's still counts as a letter here, giving HEEPS

explanation.surface: Uriah Heep in Dickens is the great hypocrite, so the comparison fits.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep, the falsely humble clerk in David Copperfield, fits the definition, but his name is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees of the Gospels were attacked for outward piety, so the name became a word for a sanctimonious fraud.

clue.text: Meal where one gets drunk with drink

parts.note: high means intoxicated
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A meal where someone gets drunk with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH TEA is a British early-evening meal of a cooked dish with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An early evening cooked meal served with tea in Britain.

clue.text: Become liable for part of the main currency

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking on responsibility for a share of the chief money in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a debt or penalty is to bring it upon yourself, becoming answerable for it.

clue.text: One taken from a TV epic perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may form another word

explanation.surface: A prisoner from a television epic, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is someone seized and held.

clue.text: Young beast embraces her, the little angel

indicators.note: the young animal wraps around the word her

parts.note: a cub is a young animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cub hugs her, the little darling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged child in art, a small angelic figure.

clue.text: He bargains for Lehar — pieces, including G duet

indicators.note: the shuffled composer's name takes the pair of letters into its middle
Lehar broken to pieces means its letters are rearranged
a duet is two performers, so the letter G is doubled

parts.note: the clue's own letter G

explanation.surface: A man haggles over the price of pieces by the composer Lehar with a duet in G.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehar wrote operettas; 'pieces' sounds musical but rearranges LEHAR to HALER, and 'including' puts GG ('G duet') inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues over a price is a bargainer at a market stall.

clue.text: Marie's follower, the one before George

explanation.walkthrough: Marie Lloyd was a famous British music-hall singer; Lloyd George was a British Prime Minister, the surname coming before George.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname follows Marie for the music-hall star and precedes George for the Welsh Prime Minister.

clue.text: Black-out of a famous racehorse

explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse blots out the sun or moon, and Eclipse was an unbeaten eighteenth-century racehorse.

clue.text: A proportion hail from Nelson

indicators.note: the hail is taken away from Nelson's first name

parts.note: Admiral Horatio Nelson
ho is a shout to hail someone

explanation.surface: A share of the greetings sent from Nelson.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson is Admiral Horatio Nelson; take the call HO 'from' HORATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses one quantity relative to another, such as three to one.

clue.text: A gentle collector carries in a plant

indicators.note: the shuffled letters carry the next word within them
a collector gathers things together in a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered collector brings home a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collector' rearranges A GENTLE to EGLANTE, and 'carries' puts IN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet briar, a wild rose, goes by this older name.

clue.text: Mark takes his off to wave

parts.note: a brand is a mark burned on

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of his are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark takes his hat off to wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name; it is BRAND. 'off' rearranges HIS to ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a sword is to flourish it in the air.

clue.text: Teachers erase many bloomers

indicators.note: the teachers rub out a letter, so erase removes it

parts.note: schoolmasters are teachers
M, the Roman thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Teachers wipe away lots of mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like blunders; it is flowers that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Michaelmas daisies and similar flowering plants are garden flowers that bloom in autumn.
